newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-DERBYSHIRE SNATCH VICTORY OVER AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DERBYSHIRE SNATCH VICTORY OVER AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Shane Warne warmed up for the first Test against England with a seven-wicket performance on Monday but could not keep Derbyshire from a dramatic one-wicket victory over the Australians.
The inspirational leg-spinner grabbed seven for 103 as Derbyshire, chasing a formidable 371 after the tourists declared on 265 for four, claimed victory with three balls to spare.

During the last over from Brendon Julian, last man Kevin Dean pushed through mid-wicket for two off the third ball after they had been gifted three off the previous delivery by a wayward throw from Greg Blewett.

Warne's performance, which earned him the man-of-the-match prize just three days before the first Test at Edgbaston, looked to have secured victory for the tourists when he trapped Andrew Harris leg before in the penultimate over.
Yet Derbyshire won it with their highest-ever score in a fourth innings and sealed their first-ever triumph over an official Australian tour side.
Derbyshire's victory may have also helped England's Test hopes as Jason Gillespie sustained a bruised left foot while Greg Blewett is still nursing a long-standing knee injury.
"The number of small injuries we have is a bigger worry than seeing a side beat us," claimed captain Mark Taylor.
"I'm not overly concerned about the result because we all got a decent bat in this match.
"It would have been nice to win but one wicket is not going to make a big difference. My main concern is having 11 guys fit for the Test match and I don't think I'm going to have that."

Chris Adams, fined 750 pounds earlier in the day by Derbyshire for openly disputing his controversial dismissal on Sunday with umpire Vanburn Holder and the Australian team, vented his anger by putting his county on course for victory with a brilliant 91 off 76 balls.

Adams, who plans an appeal to Lord's over Derbyshire's judgement, hammered 16 fours and a six to give his side a platform to mount their victory chase but after holing out to Warne at the cover boundary, the leg-spinner began to exert his influence.
Adrian Rollins, who battled for nearly two hours for 66, was trapped lbw in Warne's next over and Ian Blackwell was deceived by the slower ball to enable Warne to take a simple return catch.
Vince Clarke helped captain Dean Jones add 38 in five overs before also holing out to Julian at long-on while Karl Krikken chipped Warne to mid-wicket to set up an intriguing finish.
Needing 80 for victory with four wickets remaining, the odds seemed to be on the tourists and when DeFreitas was caught at long on to give Warne his fifth wicket, their victory seemed a formality.
Dean Jones, who had battled valiantly for two hours in compiling a vital 57, finally fell attempting a wayward slash at a wide Julian delivery and Ian Healy took a comfortable catch behind.

But after Harris departed to Warne's quicker ball, the final pair of Dean and Paul Aldred completed an unlikely victory to leave Jones admitting: "We have been a bit inconsistent in the close finishes recently at Derby but this has made up for it."

Australia, resuming on 148 for two overnight, scored quickly after losing captain Taylor in the fifth over of the day to end his hopes of a century in a first class match for the first time since his 123 against Pakistan at Perth in November 1995.
Resuming overnight on 59, Taylor hit one superb boundary through gully off Aldred before the same bowler exacted his revenge when the Australian captain edged him behind for 63.
But it was enough to convince Taylor, the subject of some stinging criticism from several former captains, to lead his side into the Edgbaston Test.
He said: "I'm going to play in the Test. This innings didn't make a difference.
"I have to play in the Test because in the lead-up we have only had two county games to get a hit and it would be unfair on blokes like Michael Slater to play without having a hit.
"I don't like the criticism I've been getting because I know these people and they are my friends. They have been put on the spot for their opinions and you can't change opinions.
"I have been sent over to captain the side and to do the job to the best of my ability for as long as I can."

Taylor's demise was the signal for Michael Bevan, resuming on 59, and new batsman Julian to launch into a boundary spree to add 101 in 15 overs as the tourists accelerated towards a declaration total.
Julian, Surrey's overseas star last season, was particularly impressive with two successive sixes off left-arm spinner Blackwell.
But after adding just 12 more runs, Julian mistimed Dean's leg-side half-volley straight to Jones, who dropped Taylor on one at slip yesterday, at mid-wicket.
Bevan was unbeaten on 104 with 14 boundaries while Warne made two before Taylor declared on 265 for four to set up Derbyshire's thrilling victory chase.
